The individual pieces were less  than 100 sq. cm. and therefore, were exempt from mentioning of batch number in  terms of regulation 2.6.1 of FSS (P&L) Regulations.

The FSO did not send the empty p a c k e t s t o t h e F o o d A n a l y s t a l o n g w i t h t h e s a m p l e . S a m e i s d i s p u t e d b y t h e L d . C h i e f P P , w h o s u b m i t t e d t h a t t h e e m p t y p a c k e t s w e r e d u l y sent along with the samples.

It is a matter of record that the Food Analyst vide his report dated 31.10.2012 recorded that :
 "......
Analysis Report:
(i) Sample Description : Sample received loose in original sealed sample bottle along  with label details which declares the sample as Costa Pesto Vegetable Parmesan Panini.
(ii) .....
(iii) Label: Without declaration of batch number.

Opinion : The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation No.2.2.2.8 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011"

bore the batch number.
The said company sold the food article in individual  packages, which did not bear batch number.

It is contended that the  i n d i v i d u a l p a c k a g e s / s a m p l e c o m m o d i t y a r e exempt from mentioning the batch number in the light of Regulation 2.6.1 FSS (P&L) Regulations, as the surface area of the package was less than 100  s q . c m s . Arun Batra V. Food Safety Officer Page No. 5 of 10 2.2.2 Labelling of Prepackaged Foods 8.
Lot/Code/Batch Identification :

A batch number or code number or lot number which is a mark of identification by which the food can be traced in the manufacture and identified in the distribution,
shall be given on the label:
Provided that in case of packages containing bread and milk including sterilised milk, particulars under this clause shall not be required to be given on the label.

6.3.2 Regulation 2.6.1 reads as under :
2.6 Exemptions from labelling requirements   1. Where the surface area of the package is not more than 100 square centimeters, the label of such package shall be exempted from the requirements of list of ingredients, Lot Number or Batch Number or Code Number, 
n u t r i t i o n a l i n f o r m a t i o n a n d i n s t r u c t i o n s f o r u s e ,
 b u t t h e s e i n f o r m a t i o n s s h a l l b e g i v e n o n t h e wholesale packages or multi piece packages, as the case may be.

6.3.3 From the plain reading of the above provisions, it is clear that mentioning of  b a t c h n u m b e r / m a r k o f i d e n t i f i c a t i o n i s mandatory as per Regulation 2.2.2.8 of FSS(P&L) Regulations.
The purpose of mentioning of the required information/ batch number on the food package is that the food can be traced to the manufacturer and can be identified in distribution, in case of violation.

However, Regulation 2.6.1  e x e m p t s a p a c k a g e f r o m d i s c l o s i n g t h e a b o v e information i.e. batch number/code number/lot number etc., which is part of a whole sale package/multipiece package and its surface area is not more  t h a n 1 0 0 s q . c m s . s u b j e c t t o t h e c o n d i t i o n t h a t t h e aforesaid details i.e. lot no., batch no.,nutritional information etc., are Arun Batra V. Food Safety Officer Page No. 6 of 10 given on the wholesale package/multi piece package.

It is a matter of record that although, this p l e a w a s t a k e n b y t h e a p p e l l a n t s b e f o r e t h e L d . A D M b u t n o s u c h wholesale package was produced before him.
6.4.1 Be that as it may.
Even if the appellants' plea is accepted for a while, such a retail package/sample package would be exempted under Regulation 2.6.1 only if its surface area is not more than 100 sq.cms.
Ld. Counsel for the appellant argued that the Food Analyst has not mentioned the surface area in his report; the surface area of the sample package is not more than 100 sq.cms.

2 I t m a y b e m e n t i o n e d t h a t t h e p a c k a g e s o f s a m p l e f o o d articles purchased by the FSO from Sh.Naveen from the premises of M/s Costa  Coffee, are available on the trial court record.
It is apparent even to the
n a k e d e y e t h a t t h e s u r f a c e a r e a o f t h e s a i d package is more than 100 sq.cms.

The same is even measured in the presence of  Ld.Counsel for the appellants and he admits that the surface area of the  sample packages on record, is more than 100 Arun Batra V. Food Safety Officer   P a g e N o . 7 o f 1 0 sq.cms.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the sample article of food was being sold by the FBO in the said packages.
Thus, the said packages are not covered under the exemption provided under Regulation 2.6.1.
In view of these facts, merely because the Food Analyst has not mentioned the surface area of the sample package and has only mentioned about the violation, does not help the appellant.

6.5 It is also significant to note that the label on the sample packages mention  d e t a i l e d i n g r e d i e n t s , n u t r i t i o n a l i n f o r m a t i o n ,
Allergen information,name of the manufacture, its address and even specifies that it is specially manufactured for Devyani International Ltd., giving its  c o m p l e t e a d d r e s s a n d e v e n p h o n e n u m b e r s .
T h e packet also gives the phone number/email for feed back/comments alongwith the timings during which such calls may be made to the consumer care  e x e c u t i v e .
N o t o n l y t h i s , t h e l a b e l o n t h e s a m p l e package has even printed upon it
Batch No.:

Mfg Date:
Best Before:
 H o w e v e r , i t d o e s n o t m e n t i o n t h e n u m b e r o f b a t c h ,
manufacturing date and the best before date.

From the above label, it is apparent  t h a t t h e m a n u f a c t u r e r w a s m i n d f u l t h a t t h e a f o r e s a i d Sh. Arun Batra S/O Sh. Raja Ram Batra vs Sh. Raj Pal Singh on 26 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100401156/
5 details needed to be mentioned on the label.
Arun Batra V. Food Safety Officer
Page No. 8 of 10 6.6

In view of  the above facts and circumstances, the appellant's plea that the sample  p a c k a g e w e r e e x e m p t u n d e r Regulation 2.6.1 from mentioning of its label no.,batch no. etc., is found untenable.
6.7 Ld. Counsel for the appellants also argued that the surface area has to be measured with the sample commodity/food article inside.
No such plea had been raised earlier.
In view of the fact that the sample package has been found to be measuring more than 100 sq.cms., mere fact that it was not measured in the packed condition, is hardly of any consequence.
Rather, when the package is filled with the food article, it would only expand further.
7.0 The appellants' have pleaded that the Ld.ADM imposed a consolidated penalty  of Rs.Three Lacs on the appellants without appreciating the provision of  S e c t i o n 4 9 F S S A c t .

entities.text: S e c t i o n 4 9 F S S A c t
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: P e r u s a l o f t h e impugned order shows that the Ld.ADM after duly considering the facts in the  l i g h t o f S e c t i o n 4 9 F S S A c t h a s a w a r d e d o n l y a consolidated penalty of Rs.Three Lacs.
The appellants have failed to make out any ground for reducing the same.

8.0 In view of the above facts and circumstances and the findings recorded in preceding paras, I find no reason to interfere Arun Batra V. Food Safety Officer Page No. 9 of 10 with the impugned order.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In view of the fact that the sample package has been found to be measuring more than 100 sq.cms., mere fact that it was not measured in the packed condition, is hardly of any consequence.
Rather, when the package is filled with the food article, it would only expand further.
The appellants have failed to make out any ground for reducing the same.

8.0 In view of the above facts and circumstances and the findings recorded in preceding paras, I find no reason to interfere Arun Batra V. Food Safety Officer Page No. 9 of 10 with the impugned order.
